Subject: Scoped processing & operator access for EU-only deployment

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the demo last week — the in-region performance looked promising. Before we move to an internal approval, Legal and InfoSec have a few specific follow-ups focused on our EU-only requirement and Schrems II / SCCs implications:

1) Can you confirm whether all inference and transient logs for our workspace can be constrained to EU-hosted infrastructure (compute, cache, ephemeral storage, and backups)?
2) For backups and disaster recovery, what are the retention defaults, and can backups be scoped to EU-only storage?
3) We need details on operator access: who (Redwood employees, subprocessor names) can access plaintext inference data in EU mode, under what circumstances, and what logging/audit evidence you can provide.
4) With SCCs in place, are there any subprocessors that remain outside the EU that would receive customer data in any form? If so, what technical/contractual mitigations apply?

Attached: MedWorks_Scope.pdf (one-page summary of the features and environment we plan to use).

Hi Eva — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below; Aditya and Naomi are looped for technical + legal specifics and to confirm evidence artifacts.

• EU-only compute and ephemeral storage: Yes — we can pin your workspace to EU regions only. All inference compute, KV cache, and ephemeral buckets used by the runtime will be provisioned in EU regions (we support multiple AZs).

• Backups & DR: Default snapshot retention is 30 days for standard clusters; backups can be configured to 0/7/30/90 days. We support EU-only backup targets (S3-compatible in-region storage). For enterprise customers we can set a restricted backup lifecycle as part of the Dedicated/Private contract.

• Operator access: By default, operator access to plaintext inference payloads is disabled. Emergency access is governed by an internal JIT (just-in-time) process requiring: documented business justification, two-person approval (SRE + Security), and full audit trail. Subprocessor list and roles are provided in our data processing addendum.

• SCCs & subprocessors: Our standard SCCs template and subprocessor roster are included in the DPA. There are a small number of non-EU subprocessors (e.g., cross-region telemetry services) but they do not receive plaintext inference content in EU-only deployments — telemetry is pseudonymized and sampled. Naomi, can you confirm the exact subprocessors and the current SCCs redline we can share?

We can produce deletion evidence: when you request purging of a workspace or model, we provide a deletion report that includes timestamps, affected object IDs, and confirmation of snapshot/backup purging where applicable. Aditya — can you add a short note on the deletion timeline for KV cache vs. backups?

Propose a short call tomorrow if MedWorks legal wants to walk the SCCs redline and evidence artifacts.

Thanks,
Michael

--
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Scoped processing & operator access for EU-only deployment

Michael / Eva — filling in the technical details:

• KV cache and ephemeral state: These are stored in-memory on GPUs and on ephemeral SSDs attached to instances in the selected EU AZs. Cache eviction is immediate; on decommission we zero memory and rotate instance disks. Forensics will show cache drop events within the runtime logs (we can include the event hashes in deletion report).

• Backups: Policy options:
  - "No backups" (we can disable snapshots entirely for the workspace)
  - "Short retention" (7 days)
  - "Standard" (30 days default)
  - "Long" (90 days)
Backups for EU-only deployments are written to EU-region object storage. Cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled by default for in-region customers.

• Deletion timelines:
  - KV cache and ephemeral artifacts: immediate on deprovision (within the same maintenance window, usually <5 minutes).
  - Runtime logs (transient): retained for 7 days by default, configurable to as low as 0.
  - Persistent backups/snapshots: deletion/expire follows the retention lifecycle; when you request immediate purge we trigger a forced deletion and return a signed deletion manifest (typically completes within 24–72 hours depending on object counts).

• Operator access / audit:
  - Access to customer plaintext is only available to a named, small operator group for emergency decode/triage. Each access event is logged in our audit system with requestor, approvers, justification, and a link to the session recording.
  - Access can be blocked entirely for Private deployments (customer-managed control plane) where we do not operate the control plane that holds plaintext keys.

• SCCs and subprocessors: Naomi to confirm list, but high-level: none of the core inference or storage substrates for EU-only mode are operated by non-EU subprocessors. Telemetry and some CI/CD tooling are outside EU but receive non-identifiable telemetry only.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix describing the deletion manifest and an example purge report for you.

—Aditya
